title: KV hit/latency/memory landscape mapping (spectra) for throughput regression detection
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Objective: Build a deterministic, reproducible harness that maps the joint space of KV hit rate, end-to-end p95 latency, and memory budget to identify throughput inflection points and enable automated regression detection. Deliver a set of spectra (memory vs hit-rate vs tokens/sec/p95) across representative workload shapes and expose them to Console dashboards and the regression CI pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can run full sweep (memory budgets, Zipf alpha, seq len dist) in under 6 hours on CI runner pool and generate artifacts (CSV + JSON)
Spectra visualizations uploaded to S3 and linked on Console experiment page with consistent schema
Regression detector flag fires when p95 increases by >15% at same tokens/sec or tokens/sec drops >10% at fixed p95 across two runs
Alerts created for CI failures with repro artifact (trace, configs, seed) and associated GitHub PR link
Bench harness is idempotent (seeded RNG) and runs produce <3% variance in tokens/sec for repeated identical config
tasks: Design workload matrix: memory budgets [64MB, 128MB, 256MB, 512MB], Zipf alpha sweep [0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2], seq len percentiles [8, 64, 128]
Implement synthetic hotset generator (zipf-backed) and integrate into existing load harness runner
Add p95 and tokens/sec collection hooks to runtime harness; include kernel selection metadata in traces
Create CSV/JSON artifact schema and uploader to artifacts S3 prefix
Wire regression detector to benchmark artifacts and add to nightly CI job
Create Console dashboard template for spectra visualization and add pre-populated experiment link

test_plan: 1) Run harness locally with single memory budget and alpha to validate metrics collection. 2) Run full sweep on CI night pool with node gating. 3) Post-process CSVs into spectra heatmaps (memory vs hit-rate -> tokens/sec & p95). 4) Run three repeats for each cell and assert variance thresholds. 5) Ingest artifacts into regression detector service; trigger synthetic regression with a seeded perturbation to validate alerting.
results_summary: Initial full-sweep (CI run 2026-03-02): 1) For skewed workloads (Zipf alpha >=1.0), tokens/sec shows a non-linear knee between 128MB and 64MB; p95 increases by ~28% at 64MB relative to 128MB. 2) For flatter workloads (alpha <=0.8), throughput degrades linearly with memory and p95 remains within 8%. 3) Kernel-selection logs indicate fallback to slower attention kernels at high miss rates, correlating with p95 increase. Next steps: validate that variance isn't harness-induced and add a focused microbenchmark to isolate kernel effect.

Publish findings to infra-announce and include recommended memory knobs for Dedicated customers
